name: Methane detection and LDAR programmes
principle: Methane leaks are found by layered detection: optical gas imaging cameras on survey rounds, drone- and aircraft-mounted laser spectroscopy for wide area sweeps, fixed continuous monitors on high-consequence sites, and handheld detectors for repair verification — all inside a leak detection and repair (LDAR) programme that logs each find, schedules repair within regulatory timeframes and closes the loop with re-survey. The driver is quantified by trackers such as the IEA Global Methane Tracker, which ties the industry's measured methane to the mitigation case.

process_steps.name: Survey layers run: OGI cameras, drones/aircraft, fixed monitors
Detections logged, quantified and screened for repair priority
Repairs executed within regulatory windows; verified by re-measurement
Emissions reported and reconciled against inventories and trackers
